observed.facings.png: Three views at one scale of a large, low, armoured scorpion-like creature in dark bronze-brown chitin with copper-orange edge highlights. South: a front view with two big pincers toward the camera, a broad faceted shield plate over the body, a dark mouth area with small fangs under the shield's front rim, and the segmented tail rising behind and curling over to the viewer's right, ending in a cluster of hooked barbs. East: a right-facing side profile with a low body under overlapping shingle-like plates, a row of spiky legs, a pincer reaching forward and the tail arching back and over with the barb cluster. North: a rear view with the shield plates seen from behind, the abdomen underside plates at the bottom, legs and the pincers' backs at the sides, and the tail rising and curling to the viewer's left with the barb cluster. No face is visible on north. The cut-out is clean on the checkerboard.
observed.south.png: A front view at full resolution. Pincers are open toward the viewer and the tips are paler and grey, slightly dusty-looking. A wide, ridged carapace shield sits above a shadowed head and mouthparts. Six to eight jointed legs splay to both sides. The tail curls over the back, and the barbed tip has 6–7 curved hooks like a claw bundle. Metallic, burnished sheen. No ground or shadow.
observed.east.png: A side profile facing right. A low, heavy body under overlapping scale plates. Spike-tipped legs point downward. The forward pincer is large, with grey-pale serrated tips. The tail is a high arc with a hooked barb cluster at the end. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: A rear view. A stacked, shingled carapace dome is seen from behind, with the ventral rear plates visible at the bottom centre. Legs fan to both sides and the pincers stick out sideways at mid height. The tail rises from the rear and curls left with the barb cluster. No eyes or face. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature spans about 2 cells wide and about 1.5 cells tall, clearly bigger and bulkier than the vanilla human. At 32 px per cell it still reads as a dark scorpion silhouette with a raised tail, much larger than the rat and wider than the human.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale on a checkerboard: a large coiled serpent with its forepart raised in a strike pose. The body is charcoal-black with cracked plate-like scales, and bright orange-red glowing seams run between the cracks. Grey ash crusts the top of the coils, and gnarled dark roots wrap around the coil. South faces the camera, east is a side profile with the head pointing right, and north shows the raised neck from behind. All three are about the same height and fill the canvas.
observed.south.png: Front view. The head faces the camera with two glowing orange eyes and an open mouth. Two long amber fangs and a red throat are visible. Behind the head the neck flares into a rounded cobra-like hood, darker and crusted with ash. The pale ventral scales of the raised neck run down the middle. The body sits in a thick coil wrapped with charred roots. Small loose ash specks float detached around the hood and the right edge. There is no ground patch, but there is also no dark outline: the edges are soft and textured.
observed.east.png: True side profile. The neck rises in an S-curve to a wedge-shaped head pointing right, with an open jaw, an orange eye and two long fangs whose tips glow amber-orange. The pale belly scales show along the inside of the curve. The coil base is wrapped with roots, and root tendrils trail off at the lower left and bottom. No hood is visible: the neck is slim in this view. A few loose ash specks float off the upper-left back.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The raised neck curves up and away, showing the back of the head and neck covered in glowing cracks. No eyes or mouth are clearly visible, though a couple of faint dark marks near the head top could be read as eye ridges. The coil base matches the other facings, with roots and an ash crust. The back of the neck shows no hood flare.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the serpent occupies about 2.5 by 2.5 cells and is roughly twice the height of the vanilla human. At 32 px per cell it still reads as a dark coiled mass with an orange-glowing raised head, clearly separate from the tan ground, though the fangs and root detail disappear.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: The head faces the camera with both eyes, open mouth and fangs visible, and the ventral neck scales face forward.

NORTH_REAR.seen: The raised neck and head are seen from behind with crack-glow back scales. No mouth or clear eyes; a faint mark near the head top is ambiguous but does not read as a face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are drawn at the oblique game camera, with the coil seen from the side and above. None is a plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Measured spread is 1%, and the three facings visually fill the same height.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Palette, cracks, roots and coil all match. However, south shows a broad cobra hood flared behind the head, while east shows a slim neck and north shows no hood, so the hood does not turn with the body.

SIGNATURE.seen: The fire-serpent identity is clear: ember glow under charred cracked scales and large venom fangs.

ALIEN.seen: The silhouette is an Earth cobra in a strike pose, hood included in south. The alien element is surface texture only (lava cracks), which reads as a recoloured cobra or a stock 'magma snake' trope rather than a new body plan.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) Charred ash-grey/black cracked scales: present. 2) Ember-orange glow between cracks: present and strong. 3) Oversized fangs glowing ember-hot at the tips: present, clearest on east (amber tips) and visible on south. 4) Coiled tight, half-buried in ash and smouldering roots: coiled with roots wrapped and an ash crust on top, which is a reasonable alpha-safe reading. The forepart is raised high rather than lying low and buried.

STYLE.seen: The rendering is highly detailed but glossy and over-saturated, with a digital-render 'lava' look. There is no clean dark outline as vanilla RimWorld has, and the edges dissolve into soft speckle. It is not cute, but it leans toward a 3D/AI render rather than painterly vanilla.

OURS.seen: Bespoke generated art matching the card. No vanilla or donor sprite.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha with no ground patch or shadow. Minor detached ash specks float around the silhouette edges (noted as polish).

SCALE.seen: The description gives no size words. At about twice human height in coil it reads as a large ambush serpent, which is plausible for a 2.5 drawSize predator.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell the dark coil with a glowing raised head is distinct from the ground. Fine details are lost but the shape reads.

reply.image_seen: facings.png shows three similarly sized charcoal serpents with orange fissures; south.png shows a frontal open mouth and broad hood; east.png shows an elevated S-shaped neck in profile; north.png shows the back without eyes; scale.png shows the coiled creature beside a human and at normal play size.

concerns.evidence: South has a broad lateral hood surrounding the head and tapering toward the chest. North shows a comparatively narrow neck below the head without the corresponding lateral expansion; east also lacks a clearly corresponding hood structure.

All three views have densely beveled scales, granular ash and intense luminous fissures with highly rendered surface lighting. The perimeter is dark in places, but its fragmented ash edges and uniformly intricate surface read closer to a fantasy render than painterly vanilla art.

The lower body forms tight coils, but the head and long neck rise prominently above them. Roots cross the exposed coils and ash collects along their tops; the body does not appear half-buried in an ash and root mat.

South has detached gray chips above and beside the hood, and east has detached chips along the upper-left neck contour. These are isolated particulate scenery, rather than a continuous background or glow halo.

The narrow slit pupils, angular scaled heads, anatomical belly plates and shaded overlapping scales do not show cute proportions, flat cel shading or toy-like simplification. The rendering concern is supported under STYLE_OFF, but STYLE_CARTOON does not describe the visible treatment.

request.prompt: A single large venomous serpent lying in a low, tight, flat coil, painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style with broad hand-painted scale masses, a clean thin dark outline around the whole silhouette, and muted naturalistic shading. Its body is covered in ash-grey and charcoal-black scaling split by an irregular network of cracks, like scorched earth, rendered as simple painted shapes rather than fine beveled scales. A restrained, dim ember-orange glow shows only in a few cracks between the charred scales, strongest along the spine, as if fire still smoulders under the skin. The head rests low near the top of the coil, at the same height as the body, a smooth, spikeless wedge with a low brow ridge, a lidless predatory eye with a narrow slit pupil, and a hard, unsmiling jaw line. The neck is a slim, smooth continuation of the body, the same in the front view with the eyes toward the viewer, in the side view, and in the rear view seen from behind showing the back of the skull and neck. The mouth is slightly open, and a pair of long curved fangs extends past the lip line, their tips glowing ember-orange. Heaps of grey ash and smouldering charred root fibres are threaded through the coils and cover much of the lower body, so the serpent reads as half-buried and waiting. All ash and roots cling directly to the scales as part of one continuous, clean-edged silhouette, with clear transparent space all around it. The creature reads at a glance as a smouldering, half-buried fire ambusher with charred cracked hide, ember light in the cracks and glowing fang tips. The sprite fills a square frame, centered, on a transparent background.
